subject: MAP: compressed acceptance window & escalation (proposal and risk log)
messages:
From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Joel Carter <joel.carter@marintech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + acceptance window: compressed eval proposal

Joel —

Quick note following last week's demo: procurement has flagged a hard cutover for internal budget reasons and they're pushing the acceptance window into a compressed timeline (targeting completion by 31 Jul). That impacts the MAP and our normal 4‑week eval cadence.

Proposed mitigation (attached: MarinTech_MAP_v3.xlsx):
- Move to a 2‑week focused evaluation (core UX + perf subset) with a dedicated Redwood canary lane for production‑like throughput.
- Daily standups for the first 10 business days, then EOD async reports.
- Pre‑defined rollback triggers (latency > 300ms p95 OR NPS degradation on prompt set).
- Temporary extended support: 24/7 pager escalation during cutover + one CI engineer on call for first 72 hours.

Risk callouts:
- Acceptance criteria need to be trimmed to a clear pass/fail, not a pass-with-conditions approach (otherwise we get scope creep).
- Legal will likely push back on SLA/credits language if the window is shorter.
- Procurement wants the SOW & test matrix before June 25 to route for approvals.

Ask:
1) Can you confirm the hard target date (31 Jul) or whether there is any tolerance?
2) Please share names/emails for your legal and procurement contacts so we can loop them into the SOW and risk log.

Attaching: MarinTech_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP draft)

Thanks — I want to be proactive here so we avoid a last‑minute stall.

— Sergio Alvarez

Joel / team —

Appreciate the clarity. I'll own the SOW runbook and tighten acceptance criteria. A few pragmatic mitigations I recommend and will include in the risk log:

Risk register (high level):
- Scope creep: reduce prompt set to 30 canonical prompts (critical path) + 10 exploratory prompts (optional).
  Mitigation: formal signoff on the 30 canonical prompts before canary start.
- False negatives on quality: create an adjudication panel (1 Marin Tech product + 1 Redwood PM) for any disputed failure.
  Mitigation: dispute turnaround within 24 hours.
- Procurement timing: approval lag could push timeline beyond 31 Jul.
  Mitigation: request expedited procurement path (we can issue a SOW placeholder while legal finishes the contract).
- Operational risk at cutover: traffic spikes exposing previously unseen latency patterns.
  Mitigation: reserve one Dedicated node group for canary and schedule a throttled ramp.

I'll attach the draft SOW and a compressed MAP risk log (SOW_redwood_v2.pdf). If Priya needs a separate security addendum (SOC2 artifacts), loop her and we'll create a short evidence pack.

Next steps I will take today:
- Finalize SOW + acceptance matrix and share for Joel's signoff by Fri (23 Jun).
- Create a succinct risk log for exec escalation if procurement can't expedite (we'll call it out to sales leadership).

— Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance window: compressed eval proposal — technical plan

Joel / team —

Technical constraints and a lighter eval harness to make 2 weeks realistic:
- Narrow the eval data footprint: pick the 30 canonical prompts that represent 80%+ of expected traffic.
- Use a pre‑warmed KV cache and controlled token budget for each test to keep latency predictable.
- Run parallel mini-load tests on Dedicated canary with 10% of peak QPS, then ramp to 50% for final verification.
- Provide a short runbook for monitoring hooks (prometheus metrics, trace ids, and nightly E2E summary).

Pass criteria suggestion (conservative):
1) Accuracy: >=95% parity on canonical prompt set (measured via blind adjudication).
2) Latency: p95 <= 275ms under 50% peak QPS for the canary lane.
3) Stability: no more than 2 incident events in the 72‑hour cutover window.

If Joel/Marin Tech accepts these criteria we can reduce test time by focusing automation on the canonical set and compressing manual adjudication to a single daily batch.

Link: Eval runbook (internal): https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/eval-compressed (for your legal team, Laura — we'll redact if needed for external).

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

1) Execute the SOW placeholder + sign DocuSign packet (link below) by July 3 so we can reserve Dedicated canary capacity.
2) If procurement/legal cannot complete full contract language by Jul 10, Marin Tech to approve a temporary operational acceptance agreement (1 page) that locks the evaluation criteria and cutover plan — legal can finalize the full SLA post‑go‑live.

From Redwood leadership: we're prepared to offer a one‑time mitigation credit equal to 30% of the first month fee if the evaluation fails only due to unforeseen infra instability (we will not apply credit for scope or data issues). This is to reduce procurement friction and accelerate approval.

If neither of the two asks above is possible, we should rebaseline the MAP to a conservative target: new close target Aug 15, 2028. I've attached a short MAP_risk_log_20280629.xlsx that summarizes the top 6 risks and suggested owners.
